newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa has signs of pneumonia, doctor says.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa has signs of pneumonia, doctor says.

text.p: Mother Teresa had signs of bronchial pneumonia on Saturday following life-saving surgery to clear two coronary artery blockages, one of her doctors said.
"She has some sign of bronchial pneumonia and we are treating that as her lung congestion is still persisting," Dr Patricia Aubanel, an American, told reporters.
Aubanel also said the 86-year-old nun's medical team planned to treat her, initially with drugs, to try to correct an irregular heart rhythm.
Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her devotion to the poor, on Friday underwent angiography and angiOplasty in a Calcutta heart clinic to clear the blockages.
Earlier on Saturday, a senior official at the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre quoted her as saying she felt fine and was ready to go home.
Aubanel, who treated Mother Teresa in California in 1991, said cardioversion treatment for an irregular heart rhythm -- sometimes done with electric shocks -- was essential.
"It is absolutely necessary now for her to go for the cardioversion to correct her irregular heart rhythm.
"There is some risk but she can't leave the hospital without this treatment," she added.
The latest medical bulletin from the clinic said: "Mother Teresa's condition remains unchanged since this morning.
"Tomorrow, the doctors will attempt to treat her arrhythmia (irregular heart rhythm). At present, she is sleeping but (she) has been cheerful and talkative all morning," it added.
An earlier bulletin said she was "doing fairly well" but was not out of danger. It said she was "conscious, alert, smiling and arguing with doctors."
On the cardioversion, Aubanel said: "Our first choice is pharmacological cardioversion because Mother Teresa had refused to have electric shocks on a couple of occasions before."
"You told me if I go through the angioplasty then you will let me go. I have gone through it. Now let me go," Aubanel quoted Mother Teresa as telling her on on Saturday.
Nuns at the Calcutta headquarters of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity order said its members worldwide planned special prayers for her on Saturday.
The Roman Catholic order, with about 4,500 nuns in more than 80 countries, was founded by Mother Teresa in 1949.
After Friday's surgery, Aubanel said angioplasty had saved the life of the 1979 Nobel Peace prize winner.
She said some danger remained to Mother Teresa's heart and it would take her up to three months to recover. She was fitted with a pacemaker in 1989.
"She was going to have a heart attack -- a major heart attack -- if the angioplasty was not done," she said.
"Mother could not have left the hospital alive without this angioplasty," Aubanel added.
Angiography is an X-ray test which uses an injected opaque dye to show up blocked arteries. Angioplasty is the procedure to unblock the artery by inserting a balloon and inflating it.
The procedures, the third time she had undergone them in five years, were performed eight days after Mother Teresa entered hospital with an irregular heartbeat.
A medical bulletin issued after the angioplasty said the angiogram had shown "blockages in two major coronary arteries".
Doctors said Mother Teresa, born of Albanian parents as Gonxhe Bojaxhi, had suffered heart failure several times since entering the Woodlands Nursing Home in Calcutta on November 22.
She was moved to the Birla clinic last Tuesday.
